title: The formal inertia extension is controlled by a class, but the quotient and action need to be retained
place: Author p.5: exact sequence and self-intersection classification sentence.
source_words: self-intersection
body: At scan096, “[self-intersection de X₀ dans 𝓧]” accompanies the claim that the tame fundamental-group extension is determined by the base and a degree-two class, with a preceding map from Π₂ᵗ to μᵗ∞. This supports Hua, findings register, `29-formal-tame-pi1-self-intersection`, and Hua’s modernised reading, “L’énoncé” (p.95), while “Lemme 2 : la classe est celle de l’auto-intersection” (p.89, outside the supplied scans) adds the proposed construction of the inertia quotient. A careful formulation must retain that quotient and its base-group action; this leaf does not prove a general central or split extension theorem.

Antecedent scans088 and090 are outside this package.
relation: frozen page supports/restates the extension–self-intersection connection in external finding `29-formal-tame-pi1-self-intersection`; earlier context adds a proposed Hochschild–Serre/Hurewicz mechanism and an explicit warning about passing from μ to its inertia quotient. It does not license calling the complete proof present on scan096.
section: Tame inertia, Kummer classes, monodromy and second homotopy

title: Arithmetic centrality is an overstatement in the context
place: Scan096 extension sequence; scan098 arithmetic examples; cancelled scan104 relation (6.4). The refuted adjective occurs in context, not scan096.
source_words: fgf^{-1}=g^q
body: The arithmetic examples of scan098 and `fgf^{-1}=g^q` on cancelled scan104 require caution with the adjective “central” in Hua, findings register, `29-formal-tame-pi1-self-intersection`, and Hua’s “La suite exacte” (p.87). For the formal disc over F₂, the tame extension F₄((u))/F₂((t)), `u³=t`, has inertia C₃ conjugated by Frobenius through inversion, so that inertia is not central. This refutes that unrestricted contextual formulation; the extension must retain its cyclotomic action, or centrality must be restricted to circumstances in which the action on the relevant inertia quotient is trivial.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote29: “La suite exacte”, Hua p.87 = scan088 (outside package), lines2306–2311: “L’extension est centrale”; repeated in `RESULTS_STATE` finding `29-formal-tame-pi1-self-intersection`. Compare “La relation, et d’où elle vient”, Hua p.103 = scan104, lines2679–2694; “L’énoncé le plus précis”, Hua pp.121–122 = scans122–123, lines3148–3167, expressly requires triviality of the Tate sheaf to remove path dependence. Hua pp.121–122 → archive scans122–123 are also outside this package; only contextual reading of that continuation was used.
relation: our direct algebraic example contradicts the context’s unrestricted adjective “central”, not the wording of scan096. The later context adds/supports the needed attention to cyclotomic twisting. A chosen basis of a Tate module does not make a nontrivial Galois action trivial.
reason: An explicit tame degree-six extension over F₂((t)) has inertia C₃ with nontrivial Frobenius conjugation; this directly refutes unrestricted arithmetic centrality in the context, while leaving the source wording intact.

title: “Extension triviale” does not follow from Π₂=0
place: Example I, first case, ending with the underlined phrase “extension triviale”.
source_words: extension triviale
body: Scan096 calls the extension “triviale” when the punctured curve is not P¹, and Hua’s “Exemple I” (p.95) repeats this as a separation of fibre and monodromy. If “triviale” means split, the stated vanishing of Π₂ is insufficient: a base with Π₂=0 can carry a nonzero central-extension class, as the Heisenberg extension of Z² shows. The useful next check is the Chern class of the normal bundle—especially its degree for a proper positive-genus curve—rather than an inference from Π₂ alone; the current package does not establish a general splitting.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote29: “Exemple I : une courbe sur un corps algébriquement clos”, Hua p.95 = scan096, lines2463–2477. Context repeats “triviale” and adds “La monodromie et le groupe fondamental de la fibre se séparent, et il n’y a rien à calculer.” Compare “Lemme 2 : la classe est celle de l’auto-intersection”, pp.89/scan090, and “Le programme kummérien : la classe, une deuxième fois”, p.100/scan101. Hua p.89 → archive scan090 is outside this package. The final unprimed D₀ on scan096 is preserved as a reading issue, not normalised.
relation: Hua restates the literal claim and adds an unwarrantedly confident splitting gloss. The logical diagnostic differs from that gloss: vanishing Π₂ eliminates a left-hand obstruction but does not itself kill the degree-two extension class. It is not a geometric counterexample to every possible hidden hypothesis from the preceding leaves.
reason: The Heisenberg extension gives a complete counterexample to the bare inference Π₂=0 implies splitting; no geometric counterexample to all implicit hypotheses of the formal-curve claim is asserted.

title: The P¹ computation needs a degree-zero convention
place: Scan096 multiplication-by-degree discussion; scan098 Example I.2, the P¹/no-boundary case.
source_words: du degré de la self-intersection
body: In the P¹ case scan098 identifies the group with μₙ, where n is the prime-to-p part of the self-intersection degree, as repeated by Hua’s “Exemple I” (pp.95,97). Conditional on scan096’s exact sequence and multiplication-by-degree map, degree zero gives the full tame Tate group as cokernel, while nonzero degree gives a finite cyclic quotient of order the prime-to-p part of its absolute value. The formula therefore needs either a degree-zero convention or an explicit nonzero-degree hypothesis; the leaf supplies neither.
context: context/hua_project/29.modern.tex — Hua, modernised reading of cote29: “Exemple I : une courbe sur un corps algébriquement clos”, Hua pp.95,97 = scans096,098, lines2478–2491. Hua repeats μₙ and then illustrates negative self-intersection `−d`, without specifying degree zero.
relation: restates the nonzero-degree formula; our observation adds the zero-degree boundary and explicitly conditions the calculation on the displayed exact sequence and the asserted multiplication map. Related state ID: `29-formal-tame-pi1-self-intersection`.
reason: The cokernel computation on the product of prime-to-characteristic Tate modules is elementary and explicit, conditional on the manuscript’s exact sequence and degree map; the geometric hypotheses themselves are not independently proved.

Hua’s “Exemple II : les entiers” (p.97) restates this open question, and his later “Le calcul” under “π₂ contre la tour des revêtements” (pp.175–176, outside the supplied scans) adds a possible approach through cohomology of covering towers. Hua’s “Exemple II” (p.97) instead paraphrases a finite-group claim “par dévissage”; this differs from the frozen reading and supplies no proof on the supplied leaf. body: Scan100 reduces the proposed semiglobal Abhyankar statement to residual-characteristic control and “Commutation des Iᵢ”, but the final local argument stops at “en un pt de”. Hua’s “Une version semi-globale du résultat d’Abhyankar” (p.99) restates the result and calls the local computation classical, which is an addition to this leaf rather than a written completion. Any reconstruction should use the revised henselian-pair hypothesis and primes invertible along the relevant divisor, and should distinguish pairwise commutation of the inertia factors from centrality under the full fundamental group.

place: Final circled 2, one-line proposed variants.

title: Cancelled quasi-unipotence lemma: the elementary ending is valid, but context changes the stated reading
place: Entire cancelled face, Lemma6.5 and unfinished eigenvalue argument.
source_words: deux automorphismes
body: On scan104, “deux automorphismes” and `FGF⁻¹=G^q` lead to quasi-unipotence, but the cancelled proof stops after choosing repeated powers of an eigenvalue. An independent check completes the argument: the finite nonzero spectrum is permuted by q-th powering, so every eigenvalue is a root of unity and a common power of G is unipotent. Hua’s “Le lemme” (p.103) supplies this ending but says the source had “endomorphismes”, a reading discrepancy with the frozen text; its account of why the page was cancelled is not established by these scans. This does not add to LM1 E.2 or close LM1 E.11, which concern group schemes over rings rather than this finite-dimensional field calculation.

title: Functorial inertia begins with dependence on a prolongation

Ce qu’est un groupe d’inertie, et de quoi il dépend” (p.116) restates this, and “2. Fonctorialité” adds the inclusion of stabilizers once an equivariant prolongation exists. Thus the research issue is to track that prolongation and its existence through a morphism, not to treat a boundary point alone as determining canonical inertia; scan117 itself does not yet prove the later functorial claims.

body: The page defines Z(G) as the set of isomorphism classes of pointed F(G)-torsors and asserts compatibility with products and equalizers by exactness of F and the rigidity lemma. It supports the torsor-based route in Hua's finding, while the categorical closure and exactness assumptions must remain attached; the later unrestricted category of all admissible S-groups is not automatically interchangeable with this setting. title: A cusp gives a minimal pointed torsor for which the broad injectivity claim fails
place: intended minimality definition, claimed injectivity and unfinished fibre product
source_words: “minimal”; “est injective”; “le produit fibré”.
body: Let A=k[x,y]/(y^p−x^(p+1)) for an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p, take the cusp point a:Spec k→Spec A, and point the α_p-torsor z^p=x by z=0. It is nontrivial and minimal among finite flat subgroup reductions, but the distinct endomorphisms 0 and [x] both push it to a pointed-trivial torsor because x^p·x=y^p; the resulting R is the nonflat normalization Spec k[z]→Spec A. This refutes the unrestricted intended assertion, while [x] is a variable S-group morphism and therefore is not a morphism of constant k-groups in the letter's example; the proposed equalizer-closed categorical restart also excludes the nonflat equalizer used here.

body: Scan107 places the completed local spectrum beside a diagram with Π₁(Z)=Ẑ² and explicitly asks for a local descent theorem and canonical homomorphisms. In the model A=ℂ[[x,y]], every finite étale cover of the full Spec A splits, so its fundamental group is trivial; the boundary complement is a different space and must be specified before invoking a two-generator inertia calculation. Hua repeats the diagram and links it to earlier completions and later descent calculations, but those contextual links do not resolve which punctures and which covering category the source intends.

title: Distinguish the line-bundle root gerbe from the divisor root stack
place: Kummer algebra and Chern target; normal-bundle class
source_words: de type Kummérien; la classe de Chern; fibré normal
body: The source's local Kummer equations and Chern-class target suggest separating two objects that Hua's later root-stack interpretation puts close together: the gerbe of roots of a line bundle and the root stack of its defining section. For X=Spec k[x], D=(x), and n>1 invertible in k, the divisor root stack [Spec k[z]/μₙ], x=zⁿ, has trivial stabilizer off D and μₙ at D, whereas the root gerbe of the trivial line bundle O_X(D) is Bμₙ everywhere. This explicit distinction refines the modern comparison and suggests tracking the section as well as the line bundle; it does not establish an equivalence with the archival covering category or a novelty claim.

title: The general Kummer programme needs a topology convention
place: allowed tame roots of unity; arbitrary n_i and degree-two class
source_words: n_i entiers ≥1; H²(X,μ_n); On veut prouver
body: Scan101 allows arbitrary positive exponents before asking for the Kummer–Chern equality, whereas the tame examples restrict the permitted residue characteristics. The Kummer sequence is exact on the fppf site for every positive n, and its usual étale surjectivity requires n invertible; the finite free root algebra and the derivative criterion verify that distinction. Hua's earlier Kummer data and later ‘Le boitement, avoué’ add the same branchwise characteristic issue, so any proof of the proposed variants should name its topology and coefficient hypotheses explicitly.

body: A useful comparison with RESULTS_STATE is to keep the test categories explicit: scan105 proposes a pro-group representing H² on finite abelian coefficient groups, whereas FINMON C2-CP2 asks about finite categories realizing a homotopy type and S2COUNT concerns maps from finite tests to spheres. Hua's ‘π₂’ and later ‘Quand un foncteur est pro-représentable’ supply a methodological link through functors and pro-objects, but they do not identify these different representability demands. title: The field-group and variable-base-group categories must remain separate
place: exact functor setup and subsequent admissible-group fibre product
source_words: exactitude de F; S-groupes admissibles; le produit fibré
body: The contrast between the letter's exact-functor setting and arbitrary admissible S-group morphisms is also the right point for a literature comparison. Antei's ‘On the bumpy fundamental group scheme’, §2.2 and §3, distinguishes finite k-group torsors from a relative base and expressly identifies nonflat group fibre products as an obstruction in the latter setting. That warning agrees with the independently checked cusp obstruction here, but it neither proves the archival restart nor resolves LM1 E.11, and no assertion about the current status of every relative fundamental-group problem is inferred from this 2015 paper.

title: Reducedness remains essential for the stated pointed rigidity
place: provisional condition (vi); Proposition3 and pointed automorphisms
source_words: essentiellement provisoires; S réduit connexe; Aut(P,ξ)
body: The kernel-uniqueness check should not be used to remove reducedness from the separate rigidity claim on scans 126 and 138. Over S=Spec k[ε]/(ε²) in characteristic p>0, the trivial α_p-torsor has distinct sections 0 and ε with the same value at its geometric point, and translation by ε is a nonidentity equivariant automorphism fixing that marking. This refutes the version with reducedness omitted and sharpens the distinction in Hua's ‘Le dispositif’ and ‘Les groupes admissibles’, while leaving the source's qualified assertion intact.
